subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — session shape, bursts & commit risk
messages:
From: Evelyn Chao <evelyn.chao@orionai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing request — quick profile

Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating a reserved/dedicated plan for a customer-facing assistant that will run our internally trained 7B decoder model (quantized to int8). High level profile below — would appreciate a preliminary ballpark and any high-risk asks you want us to answer up front.

Workload summary:
- Model: custom-7b-instruct (int8), single-turn & short multi-turn sessions
- Typical prompt: 80–160 tokens (average ~120)
- Typical response: 120–400 tokens (average ~280)
- Avg tokens per request: ~400
- Average concurrent live sessions: ~320 (business hours)
- Expected steady QPS: ~45 r/s global (US heavy), peak bursts up to 1,800 r/s lasting 20–60s during marketing events
- Session affinity: sticky sessions preferred (we maintain conversational context server-side)
- KV cache reuse: we estimate ~65% reuse for session prefix material
- SLA expectations: p95 latency goal ~600ms for standard responses; p99 should degrade gracefully (we can accept fallback to smaller model for heavy degradation)

Questions for you: what basic fleet footprint do you see for an initial commit that covers steady + typical peak bursts with safe headroom? Also list any data/telemetry we should share to make the sizing deterministic.

Attached: small token-sample CSV with per-request token counts.

Best,
Evelyn
VP Product, OrionAI
Attachment: orionai_token_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Chao <evelyn.chao@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — quick profile

Evelyn — thanks, this is a great start. A few clarifying items will materially change sizing and recommendations; could you answer the bullets below and paste together a 48h sample trace if possible (CSV or compressed telemetry link is fine). I attached our small pre-sales sizer template — dropping the numbers there will help us produce a tighter footprint.

Key clarifying questions:
- Burst shape: are the 1,800 r/s spikes back-to-back (sustained for several minutes) or short (<1 min) microbursts? What is the expected frequency (events/day)?
- Prompt distribution: you gave an average — can you provide p50/p75/p90 token counts for prompts and responses?
- Streaming: do you need partial-token streaming to the client for perceived latency improvements?
- Batchability: are incoming requests independent and batchable, or do you require strict per-session ordering that blocks batching?
- Can you share cold-start rates (new sessions/sec) vs existing session requests?
- Tolerance for fallback: you mention smaller-model fallback — what fraction of requests can be served by a smaller 2–4B model before product UX is impacted?
- Priority of cost vs latency: would you prefer fewer GPUs with more quantization & batching (cheaper) or guarantee headroom for bursts (more GPUs)?

Deliverable plan from our side (high level):
1) Quick sizing estimate (this week) based on your answers + 48h trace
2) Technical workshop (30–60m) to validate model perf and quantization profile
3) Canary plan & rollout proposal (canary -> scaled commit)

Attachment: pre-sales-sizer-template.csv (CSV, 8KB) — fill the marked cells and return.

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for fleet/ops sizing and quantization guidance.

- Markus
Director, Pre-Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Chao <evelyn.chao@orionai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@orionai.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — quick profile (details)

Markus — quick follow-up with the numbers you asked for; attached is a 48h sample (compressed). Highlights below so you don't have to dig immediately:

Burst profile:
- Peak microbursts: 1,600–1,900 r/s lasting ~30–90s, typically 3–4 times/day during promotions
- Short sustained spikes: ~700 r/s for 8–12 mins, once every 24–48 hours (batch campaign)
Prompt/response distribution (percentiles):
- Prompt tokens: p50=98, p75=135, p90=210
- Response tokens: p50=220, p75=340, p90=560
- End-to-end tokens per request p90 ~760
Session characteristics:
- New-session rate: ~20% of traffic (new session creation), rest are session continuation hitting KV cache at ~65% hit rate
- Streaming: optional — we do not require streaming for MVP; low-latency p95 is more important than streaming UX
- Batchability: requests are independent across users and can be batched at the server, but per-session order must be preserved if we do multi-turn logic (we can provide session ids)
Fallback tolerance:
- Up to 10% of requests can be served by a smaller 3B model without major UX regression; critical flows need the 7B model
Other constraints:
- Data residency: US-only (we have a FedRAMP intent later)
- Compliance: will request SOC2 report and audit logs during procurement

Attached: 48h telemetry (link) and updated token CSV. Let us know if you need any additional fields.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Attachment: orionai_48h_trace.tar.gz (gzip, 2.4MB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Chao <evelyn.chao@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — recommended next steps & proposed footprint

Evelyn — thanks for the detail and the trace; that was very helpful. Below is our initial recommended path and the main commit risks to call out. This is a pre-sales estimate — we'll refine after the perf workshop (step 2).

Executive summary (prelim footprint):
- Recommended initial reserved fleet (mixed-GPU):
  - 6 x H100-80GB nodes for peak burst absorption and p95 headroom (dedicated to heavy tail & short bursts)
  - 10 x A100-80GB nodes for steady-state throughput and batching efficiency (handles the sustained ~45 r/s comfortably)
  - Optional: 2 x T4-style worker nodes for low-cost smaller-model fallback routing (3B fallback)
- Rationale: mixed topology gives low-latency headroom for microbursts on H100s while amortizing cost on A100s for steady throughput. Quantized int8 execution with our runtime should yield ~1.5–2x throughput vs fp16 for this model family.
- Expected covered profile: steady + typical sustained spikes; will tolerate 30–60s microbursts at 1.6–1.9k r/s with autoscaling and fast-failover to fallback model when necessary.

Commit risks & mitigations:
- Risk: burst duration longer than sample (we assume 90s max). Mitigation: brief canary commit + 2-week stress test; we can add burst-only burst pool capacity if needed.
- Risk: KV cache semantics reduce batchability (per-session dependencies). Mitigation: enable prefix caching and session sticky routing; provide best-effort batching for independent requests.
- Risk: model perf variance on int8. Mitigation: perf workshop to validate quantization profile and kernel selection; fallback plan to run critical flows on 3B model if int8 accuracy regresses.

Action items / next steps:
1) Schedule 60m perf workshop with your infra + our runtime team — proposed window: week of Apr 13 (MWF mornings PT).
2) We will prepare a canary sizing run (configuration + expected p95/p99) and a follow-up quote for a 6-mo reserved commit.
3) Procurement asks: SOC2 report, KMS options for key management, and IP/traffic egress requirements (please confirm).
4) We'll share proposed quote (v1) and an ops cutover checklist.

Attached: proposed-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB) — initial numbers and options. We'll revise after the workshop.

If that plan looks reasonable, I'll book the workshop and loop our solutions architect for a short perf exercise (microbench + trace replay).

- Markus
Director, Pre-Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
